text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "SchNet uses a shifted softplus, ssp(x) = ln(0.5e^x + 0.5), as the activation function throughout the network [W2726670313#010][W2778051509#006]. The shift ensures ssp(0) = 0 and improves convergence, and the function has infinite order of continuity [W2778051509#006]. This matters for force fields because forces are obtained by differentiating the energy model with respect to atom positions, so the model must be at least twice differentiable for gradient descent on the force loss. The smooth activation gives a smooth potential energy surface [W2726670313#010]. It also gives smooth force fields and second derivatives, which are needed for training with forces and for calculating vibrational modes [W2778051509#006]. More generally, activation functions for neural network potentials must be smooth to avoid discontinuities in the forces, which rules out ReLU [W3093149769#039]."}
